content.value_statement: Debugging often fails when fixes start before evidence is understood. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through root cause analysis, pattern comparison, hypothesis testing, and verified repair.
actual_capabilities: Organizes debugging into investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation phases.
Prompts collection of error messages, reproduction steps, recent changes, and data flow evidence.
Compares broken behavior with working examples to isolate meaningful differences.
Encourages one hypothesis and one minimal test at a time.
Provides a structured debugging report template for recording evidence and results.
limitations: It guides the debugging process but does not diagnose problems without project evidence.
It depends on available logs, tests, reproduction steps, or comparable working examples.
It cannot guarantee the claimed time savings for every codebase or defect.
It may be too formal for very small or obvious issues.

use_cases.title: Investigate failing tests
use_cases.description: Use the four-phase flow to reproduce failures, compare passing cases, and verify a single fix.

use_cases.title: Document bug triage
use_cases.description: Create a clear record of symptoms, evidence, hypotheses, tests, and repair results.

use_cases.title: Control AI coding work
use_cases.description: Require Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to explain evidence before editing code.

prompt_templates.title: Start a bug investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging on this issue. First restate the symptom, then list the evidence you need before proposing any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a failing test
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the four debugging phases to this failing test. Identify the exact failure, reproduction steps, recent changes, and one first hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Compare working and broken behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for similar code paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a working example that should behave like this broken case. Compare inputs, dependencies, configuration, and data flow before suggesting a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Run a controlled repair loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Manage this debugging session with one hypothesis, one minimal test, and one fix per cycle. Stop after three failed attempts and reassess architecture.

output_examples.input: A test started failing after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The assistant records the exact error, reproduces the failure, checks the refactor, compares a passing path, and tests one hypothesis.

output_examples.input: A production workflow returns unexpected data.
output_examples.output: The assistant traces data backward from the bad output, identifies the first divergence, and verifies the fix with a focused check.

output_examples.input: Three attempted fixes did not solve the bug.
output_examples.output: The assistant stops the repair loop, summarizes failed hypotheses, and recommends reviewing design assumptions before further edits.

best_practices: Capture the exact error message and reproduction path before changing code.
Change one variable at a time and record the result.
Keep rollback options available before applying a fix.
anti_patterns: Do not patch symptoms before identifying the root cause.
Do not combine multiple speculative fixes in one change.
Do not continue the same approach after repeated failed attempts.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps debug bugs, failed tests, and unexpected behavior through a structured root cause workflow.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It describes a debugging process and relies on the assistant or user to choose approved diagnostic actions.

faq.question: Can it fix every bug?
faq.answer: No. It improves investigation discipline, but results depend on evidence, system complexity, and available tests.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Developers, QA engineers, and AI coding assistant users can use it to avoid speculative fixes.

faq.question: How is it different from normal debugging?
faq.answer: It enforces phases, evidence collection, hypothesis testing, and stopping rules before implementation.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives Claude Code and Codex a clear process for investigation before code edits.
